subject: setup
title: A useful first comparison
body: Keep the opponent, seed, and pilot policy consistent when comparing sessions. Start with enough complete games to inspect both starts, then use the replays to explain repeated decisions before changing a deck.

subject: pilots
title: What the pilot contributes
body: A pilot is a bounded layer over Forge’s decisions. Its description explains implemented behavior; its measured rate also depends on deck, opponent, build, and sample. Compare matching experiments before attributing an improvement to the pilot.

title: Make the comparison explainable

subject: results
title: Read the field before the headline
body: Check the completed-game count, both starting positions, and individual matchups before using the pooled rate. A field average can hide one difficult opponent; replay evidence is needed to explain why a result occurred.

subject: replay
title: Use the decision sequence
body: Read the turns around the decisive event, including mana, available actions, and board state. A terminal event describes how the game ended; it does not identify every earlier decision that contributed to the loss.

subject: Life Totals
title: Read the shape with the sample
body: A falling life line shows net life loss, which can include paying life. Compare the active-game counts before interpreting a late recovery: the games that ended earlier are no longer represented.

subject: Board Power
title: Pressure needs a combat check
body: A higher power line suggests a larger creature board, but tapped creatures, blockers, summoning sickness, and evasion change what can actually attack. Use the replay to check whether that board becomes damage.

subject: Creatures in Play
title: Width is only part of the board

subject: Lands in Play
title: Development is not available mana

subject: Cards in Hand
title: More cards need useful options

subject: Graveyard Development
title: A graveyard is also a resource
